prophet: One day the Prophet ﷺ was with his friends and he smiled. He told them a new surah had just come down, and he read this surah. Then he asked, 'Do you know what Al-Kawthar is?' He said: 'It is a river that my Lord promised me. It has a lot of good in it. It is also a pond where my followers will come on the Day of Judgment. Its cups are as many as the stars in the sky.' (Told by Anas, in Sahih Muslim.)

The Prophet ﷺ also told about the night he went up to the heavens. He said he came to a river with domes of hollow pearl on its banks. He asked Jibril, 'What is this?' Jibril said, 'This is Al-Kawthar.' (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim, from Anas.)

He described the river: 'It is a river in Paradise that my Lord gave me. Its water is whiter than milk and sweeter than honey.' (Ahmad, from Anas.) In another hadith he said its banks are gold and its water runs over pearls. (At-Tirmidhi said this hadith is hasan sahih.)
scholars: Ibn Abbas said: 'Al-Kawthar is the good that Allah gave to the Prophet.' (Sahih al-Bukhari.) Someone told Sa'id ibn Jubayr that people say it is a river in Paradise. Sa'id said, 'The river in Paradise is part of the good that Allah gave him.'
Ibn Kathir wrote that the word Kawthar comes from 'kathrah,' which means 'a lot.' So Al-Kawthar means a lot of good, and the river in Paradise is one part of that good.

The book Al-Jalalayn says Al-Kawthar is the river in Paradise and the Prophet's pool. It also means the many good gifts he was given, like being a prophet, the Quran, and asking Allah to help his followers on the Last Day.

Ibn Kathir explains it like this: Allah gave you so much good in this life and the next. So pray, and make your sacrifice only for your Lord. Worship Him alone. When you sacrifice an animal, say only Allah's name.
Ibn Abbas, Ata, Mujahid, Ikrimah and Al-Hasan said that 'sacrifice' means to sacrifice camels for Allah. Many other early scholars said the same.
Ibn Kathir says this is the opposite of what the idol worshippers did. They bowed to other things than Allah, and they sacrificed in a name other than Allah's.
The book Tanwir al-Miqbas (from Ibn Abbas) also gives other meanings: pray facing the Qiblah, or pray on the day of sacrifice and then sacrifice an animal.
Ibn Kathir explains: the person who hates you, Muhammad, and hates the guidance and truth you brought, he is the one who is cut off. He is the lowest person. No one will remember him.

Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Qatadah said this ayah came about Al-As ibn Wa'il. When people talked about the Prophet ﷺ, he said: 'Leave him! He has no sons. When he dies, no one will remember him.' So Allah sent down this surah.
Some scholars named other people too, like Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf, Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'ayt, or Abu Lahab. Ibn Kathir writes down all these different reports.

Ibn Kathir says they thought that when the Prophet's sons died, his name would be forgotten. That was wrong! Allah kept his name remembered all over the world, and people will follow his teaching until the Day of Gathering.
